The first one, and the most common issue I see comes with a shoulder press. We all know what a shoulder press is. It's when you're also known as a military press. You can do this with barbell or dumbbell. Um, typically it's I say that you should start this with a barbell because what you see when people are doing shoulder press is they're getting into position and they're pressing this weight up and then when they go down what they're doing is they think that they need to be flaring their elbows straight out to the side which is going to cause way too much pressure on their shoulder joint and end up causing an injury. and they go out to the side and they think that that because they feel all that tension in their shoulder, that's how they should be doing it. And this is the most common issue because this is one of the most popular shoulder exercises. So instead, what I want you guys to do, instead of putting your elbows out as far as you can, flaring them out, I want you to actually bring your elbows forward to about a little less than a 45°ree angle. And right here is a cheated rest. If I go down, perfect form, press back up, straighten my arm, lock my elbows out, I'm resting. Down, up, resting. Instead, what you want to do is really focus on not losing tension at the top of the exercise. So, you're going to go down up to the top, squeezing, getting the peak contraction of your shoulder without locking out your elbows at the top. You want to squeeze your shoulder, go right back into the next rep. Up, squeeze your shoulder, right back into the next rep. Up, squeeze your shoulder, right back into the next rep.
